answer: In a TEE-based PoA network, each agent identity is bound to a remotely attested enclave measurement, MRENCLAVE, so peers can verify the approved code is running before accepting its claims. Copying a software image cannot reproduce that identity on another virtual machine: creating another valid agent requires obtaining physical silicon and establishing a distinct attested enclave, raising the cost of Sybil attacks. The ivory, marble, and juniper labels do not alter this hardware-backed check.
